claims.text: The starting alloy has a hierarchical dual-phase lamellar microstructure containing soft FCC and hard B2 phases.
The untreated eutectic high-entropy alloy has high strength.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility.
Dislocations pile up at sharp lamellar interfaces during deformation.
Internal-stress accumulation and strain localization near phase boundaries cause cracks to propagate and coalesce along lamellar interfaces.
Controlled localized laser shock treatment will form a thin, coherent, ductile interphase layer along the lamellar boundaries.
Laser treatment will modify the local chemistry and structure of the lamellar interfaces.
The engineered ductile interphase layer will reduce the barrier strength of the lamellar boundaries.
Reduced boundary barrier strength will increase interfacial transparency to dislocations.
The modified interfaces will promote dislocation absorption or transmission.
Enhanced dislocation absorption or transmission will diminish dislocation pile-ups and local stress concentrations.
Reducing pile-ups and local stress concentrations will delay microcrack initiation.
Laser-shock-treated samples will exhibit greater room-temperature uniform elongation than untreated samples.
Laser-shock-treated samples will retain or modestly increase yield strength relative to untreated samples.
Laser-shock-treated samples will retain or modestly increase ultimate tensile strength relative to untreated samples.
Excessive laser-treatment thermal input could disrupt the lamellar morphology or introduce unwanted phases.
Non-uniform laser treatment could negate ductility gains or compromise strength.
